issues.description: The solution declares the Bookstore's stored books array as a private property (private let books: [Book]) but Client.main (in a different source file) directly accesses bookstore.books. Because 'private' in Swift limits access to the declaring file, this is a visibility mismatch that prevents the Client from reading the Bookstore's books and would cause the code not to compile. The problem description does not require the property to be private and the template does not define visibility, so this is an unintentional structural inconsistency in the solution.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the books property accessible to other files in the module (and to the Client) by removing the 'private' modifier (i.e. use 'let books: [Book]' which is internal by default) or by providing a suitable public/internal accessor (e.g. a read-only computed property or a public/internal stored property). This preserves the intended design (a Bookstore with a books array) while fixing the visibility so Client can iterate the inventory.
